StaticReview.Result: No remaining mandatory source fix identified in the reviewed integration after the queued-frame freshness correction. Runtime and recognition acceptance remain unverified.
Limits: This is source inspection only. No main firmware build, device, serial capture, labeled hand trials or physical typing trials were run by this review.

The detector identifies hands, not finger-snap posture. Any model-detected hand passing the size/region rule plus an audio transient accepted by the heuristic can still trigger one interaction. This is not posture classification or proof of a finger snap.
The geometric region is a requested large upper-central hand position, not a universal keyboard-use classifier. A keyboard hand that physically enters this region can qualify.

The state machine consumes eligibility labels, not ground-truth hand continuity. False-negative model intervals long enough to clear the region, followed by eligible detections, can create a new presentation even if a physical hand never actually left.

captured=request start is a conservative frame-age lower bound rather than a hardware timestamp. The gate's 250/100 ms intervals are evaluated on these request times. Under highly variable acquisition delays this does not prove the exact physical hold/absence duration; sensor timing and user response latency remain unmeasured.

Model/RGB destruction is ownership-safe but not guaranteed before stop returns. The camera worker must finish its current inference or DQBUF and return to its loop. The SDK DQBUF waits portMAX_DELAY; a permanently blocked driver can retain model/RGB memory and the capture mutex indefinitely. Stop deliberately waits only for microphone cleanup.
A fresh last valid in-zone frame may corroborate audio until the next model result or the 500 ms age limit. The software cannot know that the physical hand disappeared between samples.

Busy capture preserves still-fresh prior evidence. Invalid/unavailable capture failures reset the gate. A future driver/API change must preserve this distinction and the single-buffer guarantee for the flush proof.
When camera_required is explicitly disabled, the configuration intentionally bypasses the hand gate.

The earlier standalone MSVC C++17 /W4 /WX hand_gate_test run passed 17 synthetic test groups, including 4 motion-only eligible windows versus 0 rearmed windows after consumption. This does not test the current camera/service integration or establish real recognition accuracy.
Model initialization preflight and exception checks do not eliminate every vendor allocation/assert failure path; this remains documented in hand_model.cpp.
